hypotheses.title: Inferring the type of a mapping constructor with no expected type is O(fields^2) in stage 5 (combineMappingConstructorShape visits every member for every name)
hypotheses.issue: When a mapping constructor has no contextual type (e.g. `var m = { f0: 0, ..., fN: N }`), resolveMappingConstructorBottomUp calls combineMappingConstructorShape. That function loops over every distinguished name (mappingMemberNames). For each name it loops over every member and calls mappingConstructorMember.contribution(name) and mappingTypeInhabited (t.typeContext() + semtypes.IsEmpty). With N specific fields only one member supplies each name, yet all N members are visited: N^2 contribution calls and N^2 IsEmpty calls. For a spread member, contribution() also scans its fields linearly, which gives O(names x members x spreadFields). The function is also used on the expected-type spread path (checkMappingConstructorSpreads). possibleMappingConstructorShape.isOptional and isReadonly use slices.Contains over slices, and inferMappingConstructorType calls them once per name, which adds a second quadratic term. On a 16000-field literal, Local Type Resolution takes 4.6 s of 5.1 s wall time. The same literal with an explicit map<int>/record{} type takes about 0.15 s.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a .bal file whose main() binds one large mapping constructor to `var`.

The constructor has no contextual type, so stage 5 infers it bottom-up via
resolveMappingConstructorBottomUp -> combineMappingConstructorShape, which is
O(fields^2). Usage: gen_var_mapping.py N > out.bal
"""
import sys

n = int(sys.argv[1])
fields = ",\n    ".join(f"field{i}: {i}" for i in range(n))
print("import ballerina/io;\n")
print("public function main() {")
print(f"    var config = {{\n    {fields}\n    }};")
print("    io:println(config.length());")
print("}")
reproducer.command: python3 gen_var_mapping.py 8000 > var_mapping_8000.bal && go build -o /tmp/bal ./cli/cmd && /usr/bin/time -f '%e s %M KB' /tmp/bal run var_mapping_8000.bal ; ./bin/benchmark --mode time --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> var_mapping_8000.bal

hypotheses.baseline: main wall time / peak RSS: N=4000 0.40 s / 61 MB; N=8000 1.40 s / 85 MB; N=16000 5.07 s / 131 MB; N=32000 20.4 s / 222 MB. Time roughly quadruples each time N doubles. Local Type Resolution is 4.6 s of the 5.1 s at N=16000.

improvement.summary: Wall time on the 8000-field reproducer dropped 83% (1399 ms -> 236 ms, benchmark tool; hyperfine shows 5.76x faster). At 16000 fields: 5.07 s -> 0.53 s. At 4000 fields: 0.40 s -> 0.10 s. Peak RSS is unchanged (the memory benchmark marks it unreliable, CV 4.2%, +2%, within noise).

hypotheses.fix_approach: Before the per-name loop, combineMappingConstructorShape builds an index once: specific-field members by name (map[string][]int), the list of spread member indices, a per-spread map[string]MappingField so a spread's field lookup is O(1), and whether each spread's rest type is inhabited (IsEmpty computed once per spread, not once per name). The spread rest union also moves into this first pass. For each name, the loop visits only the specific fields written with that name plus the spreads. These are sorted by member index, so unions are built in the same order as before and the inferred types are unchanged. t.typeContext() is called once, outside the loop. optionalFields and readonlyFields become map[string]bool sets, so isOptional and isReadonly are O(1). The order these fields are inserted never mattered, because output order comes from shape.names(), which is sorted. Pitfall: keep the semantics where an uninhabited contribution is skipped but a specific field still counts as guaranteed, and where a spread guarantees a name only through a non-optional field. With many spreads the work is still O(names x spreads), but that is no longer quadratic in the field count. make test passes.

notes: Validation found a smaller quadratic in Semantic Analysis on the same reproducer: validateMappingConstructor -> semtypes MappingAtomicType.FieldInnerVal/FieldCell does a linear field lookup per field (about 0.26 s at N=16000). That overlaps the 2026-10-28 report and was not pursued.
